description.narrative: Oour Voices Our Futures (OVOF) will use capacity-building and convenings among feminist movements to strengthen and build movements within countries and across regions, while also link feminist movements to relevant actors, such as internet rights’ movements, Dutch allies and progressive policymakers. OVOF believes in strengthening movements from within, to create more inclusive, powerful and resilient movements. To influence laws and policies at national and international levels, OVOF sees this as the only sustainable mitigation strategy in relation to the increasing power of anti-rights and anti-gender forces.

Partners efforts led to (1) emergence of a nascent network of feminists and activists from the MENA/SWANA region, which is particularly significant in a region where queer and feminist organizing can be politically constrained, and where safe cross-border exchanges are rare; (2) initiated archiving of knowledge products of an OVOF partner on issues of democracy, sexuality etc ; (3) conducted a strategic retreat and discussed the precarious nature of the funding system, collectively setting strategies that are realistic and based on collective feminist aspirations and principles, which is very important for a sustainable efforts.

Two feminist journalism workshops by an OVOF partner supporting women and queer writers resulted in multiple published pieces and examined the gendered politics of residential design, resonating widely across the region for its nuanced exploration of how physical spaces reproduce emotional and mental confinement for women. In addition, a successful partnership between CREA and a regional feminist learning institution was formalised providing a regional feminist and queer learning space for critical discourse in Arabic, on issues of gender and sexuality, and for the development of a contextual localised feminist learning curriculum.
Due to the conflict in the region, a decision was taken to not proceed with activities on the ground in 2023.
